title: Sneeze Count and Seasonal Peaks
dataSources: Posture readings (`posture:reading`), symptom logs (`symptom:log`), bathroom visits (`bathroom:visit`), sneeze events (`sneeze:event`).
app: Everyday body-signal logs — posture sensors, symptom and allergy journals, hydration-linked bathroom logs, and quirky personal counters — sent to Splunk HEC via wearables, MQTT, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=sneeze:event
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(count) as sneezes by _time
| eventstats avg(sneezes) as typical
| eval peak=if(sneezes>typical*2,1,0)
| sort - _time
description: Counts your daily sneezes and flags the peak days, a quirky but real window into allergy season.
value: A sneeze count is playful, yet its seasonal peaks map neatly onto pollen spikes and help time antihistamines.
implementation: Log sneezes (a counter button) into `index=personal`; flag unusually sneezy days.
visualization: Column chart of daily sneezes with peak days marked.
grandmaExplanation: It counts your sneezes each day and flags the worst ones, a fun peek at your allergy season.
